<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**34** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 146b6f9b6018b8144690338cf1cf0374407a4187`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (symbol, 56 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 56 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **3** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 146b6f9b6018b8144690338cf1cf0374407a4187` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a6e95a80a673a240018f63b6a79a0df570ee6024` — the merge of head `e06f4b85bf4d8d65aefdc4aaee3cd54992f05102` into base `146b6f9b6018b8144690338cf1cf0374407a4187`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a6e95a80a673a240018f63b6a79a0df570ee6024 && git checkout a6e95a80a673a240018f63b6a79a0df570ee6024
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 146b6f9b6018b8144690338cf1cf0374407a4187 e06f4b85bf4d8d65aefdc4aaee3cd54992f05102 && git checkout -B drift-repro 146b6f9b6018b8144690338cf1cf0374407a4187 && git merge --no-ff e06f4b85bf4d8d65aefdc4aaee3cd54992f05102

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 146b6f9b6018b8144690338cf1cf0374407a4187
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 146b6f9b6018b8144690338cf1cf0374407a4187` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — REWORK · head 30de59af71b9b50420784f2a4836eb628ccfca42 (one test-only item; the rest is ACCEPT-ready)

**REWORK item:**

1. `packages/runtime/src/platform-admin-action-gate.test.ts`, new case "a plain member is refused 403 at the door …": the refusal asserts `status` 403 and message text, but not the envelope `code` (ADR-0112; l1-review-checklist, "rejection cases assert `code` and `status`"). Add the code assertion on the REST refusal body. It should be `PERMISSION_DENIED`, which the file's own MCP twin pins for this gate. After the push I read only that delta.

**What I checked, which carries to the ACCEPT:**

- **Shape:** `l1-face.mjs --pr 36162` at 30de59af71: open, draft, base main; first line `Fixes #36017`, which delivers the card (read back the manager plus direct reports, seeded Set Manager, and a clear); no closing keyword on any other card; `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`.
  - Its one flag, a changeset missing for `@objectstack/runtime`, is not a defect. The only runtime file touched is `src/platform-admin-action-gate.test.ts`, and runtime's `files` is `["dist","README.md","CHANGELOG.md"]`, so nothing in runtime ships from this PR. `@objectstack/platform-objects` carries the changeset.
- **(1) Field-backed `managerId` on the readonly `manager_id`, checked in code:**
  - `ui/packages/fields/src/resolveActionParams.ts` returns, for a field-backed param, `name`, `label`, `type`, `required`, `options`, `placeholder`, `helpText`, `defaultValue` (row first), `visible`, `carryOver`, `widget`, `multiple`, `accept`, `maxSize` and the lookup extras. It never copies `readonly`.
  - `paramToField.ts` and `ActionParamDialog.tsx` neither read nor pass `readonly` (there is no `readonly=` prop in the dialog), and `LookupField` goes display-only only on its `readonly` prop.
  - So the picker stays editable, and the stale warning on main is rightly rewritten.
  - The row seed reaches list rows through `ui/packages/core/src/utils/predicate-fields.ts` (since objectui#10277 it harvests the field a `defaultFromRow` param seeds from).
  - Not measured in a browser: neither the dev nor I opened the dialog.
- **(2) `remove_user_manager`:**
  - `visible` is `set_user_manager`'s standing term followed by `&& has(record.manager_id) && record.manager_id != null`. That is the Ban/Unban row-state form, and the test pins the `startsWith(standing + ' && ')` prefix, the single `record.manager_id` column and the sparse-row `false`. I accept it as the declared deviation: it hides the action only when there is nothing to remove, and the server gate is unchanged.
  - The null survives both console doors: `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` does `Object.assign(body, resolvePageVarTokens(bodyExtra))`, whose `walk` returns `null` as is, and `RecordDetailView.tsx` does `Object.assign(body, action.bodyExtra)`, both before `JSON.stringify`. The server door is pinned by the new runtime test (`managerId` present and `null`).
  - The endpoint, `plugin-auth/src/admin-set-user-manager.ts`, applies refusal 5 (SCIM-held) before the `managerId !== null` screen, so the changeset's "refused there for the clear too" is true.
  - No `ai` block, the same `requiredPermissions` and the same locations as Set Manager.
- **Changeset, read sentence by sentence:**
  - "Details tab named no section holding `manager_id`": origin/main `sys-user.page.ts` has no `manager_id`.
  - Reporting Line / Direct Reports, the `defaultFromRow` seed, the request body unchanged, Remove Manager's gate, its confirmation, no AI exposure, and the SCIM refusal all match the diff.
  - The 11 `*.objects.generated.ts` bundles each add the same three keys.
- **Gates:** 37 success, 16 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending at 30de59af71. Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are both success.
- **Landing, once the item is in:** not governed, under 3,000 lines, `Clause-②: no`, no contract record owed. The area lands it.
